subject: Read and write machine-bound connection files
body:
Read and write machine-bound connection files

Adds the file format for master-keyed files. Nothing creates one yet, so
existing files are untouched and behaviour is unchanged; migration comes next.

The write path was not a choke point: each serializer version encrypts every
secret itself through ICryptographyProvider, passing the file password. Rather
than rewrite all of them, MasterKeyCryptographyProvider carries the already
recovered master key and ignores the password argument, so every existing call
site keeps working while the per-secret key derivation disappears.

- KeyProtection/ProtectedKey attributes on the Connections root record the mode
  and the wrapped key. Recorded rather than inferred: the two ciphertext forms
  differ (the password form prepends a per-secret salt), so a reader has to know
  which it holds before decrypting.
- CryptoProviderFactoryFromXml returns a master-keyed provider when the file
  says Dpapi. The lookup sits outside the existing catch on purpose: that catch
  means "unreadable header, assume an ancient Rijndael file", which is right for
  a missing attribute but wrong for a file that declares machine binding and then
  cannot produce its key. That must be reported, not degraded into what would
  look like corruption.
- Files with no KeyProtection attribute keep taking the legacy password path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

triage.rationale: DPAPI-wrapped master key fixes mR3m weak-default (our #128/incident #92 concern). Real value, but new file-format attribute, compat + serializer conflicts with our 1600-commit divergence. Reimplement deliberately if pursued.

votes.concern: Standalone import cannot compile: it depends on missing parent key-protection primitives and keyed AEAD APIs.
votes.reason: The fork already solves KDF cost through 600,000-iteration caching, while this stale patch conflicts with certificate, TOTP, and serializer changes.

votes.concern: Breaks connection file portability across different machines/users and introduces merge/compatibility conflicts due to serializer changes in our heavily diverged codebase.
votes.reason: Addresses critical default password weakness, but breaking file portability and causing serializer conflicts requires deliberate human decision and custom reimplementation.
